findings.title: Email blocks can be bypassed by changing address casing
findings.body: The blocked-email lookup uses case-sensitive equality, and neither BlockedEmail nor User normalizes the address before this lookup. For example, blocking `block@spamfromhome.org` still allows signup with `block@SPAMFROMHOME.ORG`, which identifies the same mailbox because domain names are case-insensitive. Normalize stored blocked addresses and lookup values consistently with the application's email handling so casing cannot bypass a block.

findings.title: Concurrent matches lose counter increments
findings.body: The match counter is updated by reading a record, incrementing its in-memory value, and saving it without locking. Two concurrent requests matching the same blocked address can both read a count of N and both save N+1, recording only one of the two matches. Use an atomic database increment or lock the record while updating the statistics to keep match_count accurate under concurrent signup attempts.
